title: Recover the existing MCP session after a transient daemon handshake timeout
outcome: A transient daemon_handshake_timeout must not permanently strand an existing MCP session in UnavailableMcpShim after the daemon becomes responsive; recover without restarting the agent or rebuilding the index.
acceptance: A deterministic end-to-end regression initializes an MCP session after a forced authority-handshake timeout, then allows the daemon to respond and proves a subsequent tool call succeeds through that same MCP session and proxy process.
Continued daemon unavailability remains honestly reported; recovery preserves MCP initialization and request/response correlation without replaying already-dispatched mutating calls.
Recovery requires neither daemon/index restart nor longer handshake deadlines; full quality gates and adversarial review pass.

completion.summary: Same initialized MCP session recovers from transient handshake failure through an existing daemon, without restart, rebuild, deadline changes or replay. Added transport/result-loss recovery, phase-aware protocol handling, correlated cancellation, relay shutdown cleanup, and unavailable capability disclosure. Decisive RED/GREEN, full gates and original dual verification complete.
